result:
I found 11 rules whose code didn't match their docstrings and fixed all of them in `pricebook.py`. After the fixes, I re-ran a check that compares every rule (1–150) against its docstring across many quantity and unit-price combinations, and nothing mismatched.

| Rule | What was wrong | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 11 | Discount started at 13 units, not 12 (`qty > 12`) | `qty >= 12` |
| 18 | The 100,000 won cap only applied once the discount went over 200,000 | Always cap at 100,000 |
| 28 | A "whole" rule was discounting only units above 50 | Discount the full amount (`base * 5 // 100`) |
| 44, 79, 139 | `round()` rounded the discount instead of flooring it to the won | Changed to `// 100` |
| 65 | The 30,000 won cap was applied to the price before the discount, not to the discount | Cap the discount itself |
| 91 | Discount started at 13 units, not 12 | `qty >= 12` |
| 105 | Used 9% instead of 8% | Changed to 8% |
| 119 | Discount started at 31 units, not 30 | `qty >= 30` |
| 127 | Discount started at 31 units, not 30 (`qty > 30`) | `qty >= 30` |

Rule 15 uses `qty > 100` instead of `>= 100`, but I left it alone. It's a "marginal" rule, so the discount at exactly 100 units is 0 either way and the result is the same.

STATUS: DONE
